title: A space boost on an indoor set-point entity holds the plan's partial set-point, not the band top
claim: With Boost Space Heating live on a partial step and an indoor space set-point entity, the pump holds optimal_setpoints[K] = 21.0 C while the boost's own action asks max_temperature 23.0 C, on 2 of 2 indoor rigs; the water rigs write the top (55 C).
mechanism: pump_arbiter.desired passes boosted only for a water unit ('The boost fact is read for a water set-point only'); _space_target's indoor branch reads _planned_room(result, now), the plan's step, while boost.overlay replaced the action's setpoint with max_temp. The boost lifts the supply switch and mode but never the indoor set-point, so the pump's own thermostat stops at the plan's partial target.

evidence.unit: rigs (fork-indoor, gchv-indoor) whose boost-partial set-point lies between floor and top
evidence.machine: box B11, Linux 6.18.44 x86_64, venv-ci CPython 3.14
evidence.contention_note: count; contention-immune (two other seats on the box)

perturbation.change: --perturb boost_indoor: desired maps an indoor set-point under a live space boost to max_temperature

metric_definition: Rigs whose indoor space entity, after the boost-partial step's writes, reads other than max_temperature (the boost overlay's setpoint).
phenomenon_property: Under a live space boost the space channel's target is the top of its band on every space set-point unit, never the plan's partial level.

null_control.note: the flow rigs' boost-partial rows hold 55 C = the band top (rows ok); the indoor partial rows without a boost hold optimal_setpoints[K] (rows ok)

proposed_fix_scope: pump_arbiter.desired/_space_target: an indoor unit under a live space boost (or MODE_BOOST) writes the boost's setpoint (max_temperature on the entity grid).
